title: closed-loop identity exact-match live evidence package
policy: read-only: the SQLite store was opened with mode=ro; no writes, no apply, no broadcast. No rotation probe is performed because the system has no rotation behaviour to measure.

identityModel.closedLoopIdentity: funding anchor + directed pool path (ordered address path)
identityModel.lookup: exact match on the ordered 3-address path, case-normalised
identityModel.rotationProbeRationale: No rotation probe is run: the system has no rotation lookup, so there is no observable rotation behaviour to measure. A 'rotated path must not hit' check would rest on a false premise and is deliberately absent.

rotationCapabilityAudit.method: static source-level capability audit over 1161 Rust/Python files
rotationCapabilityAudit.verdict: no closed-loop rotation lookup, rotation normalisation, rotation alias merge or canonical rotation definition or call exists in the Rust kernel, the Python runtime or the tool layer
rotationCapabilityAudit.note: the audit is a capability guard, not a behavioural assertion: hit-or-miss on a rotated path is not an acceptance item, metric or test assertion, and none exists

3_match_result.verdict: every published loop resolves to exactly one catalogue entry under its own ordered address path; no path conflict, no miss, no key drift

4_miss_diagnosis.note: no miss occurred in this run, so no identityMismatch repairTarget was emitted; the repairTarget=closed_loop_manager branch is covered by the Rust regression suite instead

5_real_review_consumes_manager_original_.verdict: every real review consumes the Manager published identity verbatim on loop_key and ordered address path, and every review carries a positive measured capacity; the ordered pool set agrees for 40/44 and differs for 4/44 because those reviews predate the current Manager publication (stale snapshot), not because of an identity defect

6_same_basis_reconciliation.verdict: 44 manager reviews map onto 44 distinct Manager closed loops; no Manager loop is split into several Python identities and no extra identity is produced

staleReviewPoolSet.mechanism: the 4 affected reviews were reviewed at 2026-11-19T05:26Z while the current Manager publication for those loops was written at 2026-11-19T11:39:20Z. manager_v4_closed_loops.backup_pool_ids_json shows the previous hop split, and the current pool set moved the 0x2bca43d9... pool from the third hop to the first hop. The reviews therefore carry the previous publication's pool set.
staleReviewPoolSet.whyItIsNotAnIdentityMismatch: the ordered address path and loop_key agree with the Manager for all 44/44; only the pool set of the 4 oldest reviews lags the publication
staleReviewPoolSet.whyItIsNotFixedSilently: the readings are reported as observed; no pool set is rewritten, back-filled or defaulted, and no capacity/pool/valuation is borrowed from another loop

orphanRuntimeStateRows.handling: diagnosed precisely and left unassociated with any closed loop; no capacity, pool, USDG valuation or threshold is taken from them
